question: Why do horses call the incomparable lord with their neighing sounds?
premises: Horses call with distinctive neighing sounds.
They invite the deity to mount them.
They regard him as their incomparable own lord.
inference: The horses express devoted service by offering themselves as mounts to their supreme lord.
plain_english: With their neighing sounds, they call you, the incomparable lord, to mount them as their own master.
